newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief favors multinational force for E. Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief favors multinational force for E. Zaire.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali threw his support Friday behind the dispatch of a multinational military force to deal with a looming catastrophe in eastern Zaire, where more than a million refugees are without food and medical care.
"Given the need for urgent action if tens of thousands of lives are to be saved, times is of the essence," he said in a letter to Security Council President Nugroho Wisnumurti of Indonesia.

Boutros-Ghali said it would take too long to deploy a U.N. peace-keeping force or one set up by countries in the region, and the best option would be if U.N. member states "with the necessary capacity would take the lead in putting together a multinational force, in consultations with the secretary-general of the OAU (Organization of African Unity) and the regional states concerned, and would seek the Security Council's authorisation to deploy it."
Boutros-Ghali, whose letter was dated Thursday, said he therefore welcomed the fact the council was "focusing its attention on this option."

This was a reference to a resolution circulated by France that would authorise the establishment of a multinational force for two months to allow the safe delivery of aid to refugees and others at risk in eastern Zaire.
The resolution was being discussed by council members during closed-door consultations Friday but there was no immediate indication when it might be adopted.
